entries.label: Biological Machines
entries.quote: Michel Maharbiz's novel interfaces between machines and living systems could give rise to a new generation of cyborg devices.

entries.label: $100 Genome
entries.quote: Han Cao's nanofluidic chip could cut DNA sequencing costs dramatically.

entries.label: Paper Diagnostics
entries.quote: George Whitesides has created a cheap, easy-to-use diagnostic test out of paper.
entries.note: Body text timing: "around the end of this year".

entries.label: Traveling-Wave Reactor
entries.quote: A new reactor design could make nuclear power safer and cheaper, says John Gilleland.

entries.label: Racetrack Memory
entries.quote: Stuart Parkin is using nanowires to create an ultradense memory chip.

entries.label: Liquid Battery
entries.quote: Donald Sadoway conceived of a novel battery that could allow cities to run on solar power at night.

entries.label: Intelligent Software Assistant
entries.quote: Adam Cheyer is leading the design of powerful software that acts as a personal aide.

entries.label: Nanopiezoelectronics
entries.quote: Zhong Lin Wang thinks piezoelectric nanowires could power implantable medical devices and serve as tiny sensors.
entries.note: Body text timing: "five to ten more years".

entries.label: HashCache
entries.quote: Vivek Pai's new method for storing Web content could make Internet access more affordable around the world.

entries.label: Software-Defined Networking
entries.quote: Nick McKeown believes that remotely controlling network hardware with software can bring the Internet up to speed.

notes: Ten entries, each framed around one researcher. No availability field. Forward timings from body text are in entry notes. Read through a summarising fetch; medium confidence.
